hypothesis: The known-good 116188 training file can complete Neuron startup from a truly isolated empty compile cache on trn22. A repeated pre-model RNG/NEFF failure would implicate shared cold-start setup more than an S0-only model defect, but one binary contrast cannot prove a root cause.
single_causal_change: Use the previously successful 116188 bytes and exact historical dense launch flags on trn22, while deliberately isolating all compiler caches—including the AWS-documented persistent cache URL—in fresh empty job-owned directories. This tests cold-start feasibility; no science change or quality adoption is proposed.

Tests S0 native startup on an authenticated populated cache, but cannot establish scorer cold-start safety.

success_criteria.quality: Informational public20M only; no cross-host quality adoption or S0 submission decision from this contrast alone.
success_criteria.throughput: Record startup duration, steps and charged training time. Cold compile must remain within competition semantics and produce a loadable checkpoint.
success_criteria.correctness: Full-chip four-rank 1800 s run, finite model-only checkpoint, strict load, no NaN/crash/budget breach, verified effective cold cache path with new files under the precreated empty NEURON_COMPILE_CACHE_URL after first compile, and fresh-process public20M. If effective cache isolation is not proven, label result inconclusive as a cold-cache test.

abort_conditions: Trn22 A0 still active, any Neuron/device holder or STOP, disk free <6.5 GiB, unique label/root already exists
Any cache directory not empty before launch or effective persistent-cache path not proven; do not infer cold from NEURON_COMPILE_CACHE_DIR alone
Source/prepare hash or dense launch argv mismatch, crash, NaN, missing checkpoint, budget or eval failure
